messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: major holes in existing fwd-mode
parts:
I realized when writing the new tests for diag_post_multiply
that it was only written for fvar * fvar, not for double * fvar
or fvar * double. I'm guessing from this that it's a widespread
problem that was never caught in the original testing.

This means there's a lot more work to do to get the existing
forward mode working.

I can add implementations for these and then fix the tests,
but is that the right thing to do? It's certainly the path
of least resistance for me to get by our testing requirements.
Although the truly least path would be to sneak by a test that only
tested fvar * fvar, which now works, but I like to stay honest here
and try to do what's expected of me.

One option would be to just rip out all the forward mode we
currently have in anticipation of the new one. But I want
to have the current one around for testing.

Also, if we're going to use the current version, it should
really be updated to deal with mixed types:

template <typename Tval=double, typename Td=Tval>
struct fvar {
Tval val_;
Td d_;
}

This would make all the second-order calculations go much faster.

- Bob
